newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Babcock says may cut 10,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: D.Babcock says may cut 10,000 jobs.

text.p: Troubled German engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG said on Tuesday that it may cut up to 10,000 jobs through restructuring measures and the sale of subsidiaries.
"About half of the reductions will come from job cuts and the rest through the sale of subsidiaries," newly-appointed chief executive Klaus Lederer told a news conference.
Lederer added that "a great deal" of management jobs would be affected by restructuring. He did not give a timetable for the shedding of workers.
Numbers released earlier on Tuesday showed Babcock planned to reduce its workforce to 28,500 this year and 28,000 next year from 32,300 at the end of the 1995/96 business year.

Lederer took over as Babcock CEO in January after the departure of Heyo Schmiedeknecht, who led an acquisition spree which ended up dragging the group deep into the red and straining bank credit lines.
The company said earlier it had trimmed group net losses in the first four months of the current business year by 100 million marks ($58.7 million) from a year-ago loss of 250 million marks.
Babcock also said it expected to halve its pre-tax loss in the current year to September 30 and break even in 1997/98. Group pre-tax losses last year were 400 million marks.
